title: eBook | What do utilities and power developers need to know in H2 2026?
gist: A Wood Mackenzie promotional page for an eBook on five H2 2026 power-market trends: networks, demand-driven generation mix, solar and wind opportunities, supply-chain costs and energy security. It offers themes but no data.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says networks are moving to the heart of utility investment, with opportunities differing between markets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Grid investment is a priority theme for utilities and related equipment suppliers.

insights.claim: Rising electricity demand could reshape the generation mix, increasing the need for renewables, storage and flexible generation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Demand growth supports a broad set of generation and storage assets.

insights.claim: Supply-chain changes, including localisation, tariffs and commodity and freight pressures, are affecting power project costs and procurement.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Project cost inflation risk from trade policy and commodities should be monitored.

insights.claim: Energy security is becoming more important to power-sector investment decisions as geopolitical disruption affects fuel and equipment markets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Security-of-supply considerations favour domestic and diversified supply chains.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie argues generation, networks, storage, fuel supply and procurement decisions are increasingly interconnected, so single-technology analysis is no longer enough.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Favours integrated cross-market analysis over technology silos.
